reasoning_content: The caller doesn't pass persistence directly - it's injected via dependency injection in WorldTick constructor. Let me check how persistence gets injected.

action.command:
cd /workspace/project && python3 << 'ENDOFSCRIPT'
import paramiko
client = paramiko.SSHClient()
client.set_missing_host_key_policy(paramiko.AutoAddPolicy())
client.connect("46.202.154.25", 22, "root", "2N00py123+++")

# Check how WorldTick gets persistence - DI or manual?
stdin, stdout, stderr = client.exec_command("grep -n 'persistence' /opt/areloria/server/src/core/ServerBootstrap.ts | head -10")
print("Bootstrap persistence:", stdout.read().decode())

# Check for injection patterns
stdin, stdout, stderr = client.exec_command("grep -n '@Inject' /opt/areloria/server/src/core/WorldTick.ts 2>&1 | head -5")
print("\nInject:", stdout.read().decode())

# Check if there's a DI system
stdin, stdout, stderr = client.exec_command("head -50 /opt/areloria/server/src/core/ServerBootstrap.ts")
print("\nBootstrap start:", stdout.read().decode())

client.close()
ENDOFSCRIPT
